answer: At a harbor tracking a smoke plume near a willow inlet, each paid report needs a one-use ferry manifest token issued after a sensor package crosses the quay. The exchange redeems each token once and checks its serial against dock cameras. Many accounts cannot multiply one crossing; an attacker needs separate packages, ferry fees and time for every extra claim. A bribed dock operator could issue phantom tokens, so a second operator reconciles camera counts and random packages are inspected. Remote agents can hire a carrier, but wealthy attackers can still buy many crossings.
